text: John William Robert Kerr, 7th Marquess of Lothian PC (1 February 1794 – 14 November 1841), was a Tory politician who styled himself Lord Newbottle from birth until 1815 and held the courtesy title Earl of Ancram from 1815 to 1824. He served briefly as Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard under Sir Robert Peel between September and November 1841. Kerr was the eldest son of William Kerr, 6th Marquess of Lothian, and Lady Harriet, daughter of John Hobart, 2nd Earl of Buckinghamshire. He entered the House of Commons in 1820 as one of two representatives for Huntingdon, a seat he held until he succeeded his father as Marquess of Lothian in 1824. He also succeeded his father as Colonel of the Edinburgh Militia, a position he held until his death. In September 1841, he was sworn of the Privy Council and appointed Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard in Sir Robert Peel’s Tory administration, a role he held until his death in November 1841. He served as Lord-Lieutenant of Roxburghshire from 1824 to 1841. In 1831, he married Lady Cecil Chetwynd-Talbot, daughter of Charles Chetwynd-Talbot, 2nd Earl Talbot; they had five sons and two daughters. Their two elder sons, William and Schomberg, both succeeded to the title. Their third son, Lord Ralph Kerr, became a major-general in the army and was the father of Philip Kerr, 11th Marquess of Lothian; their fourth son, Lord Walter Kerr, became an admiral in the Royal Navy and was the grandfather of Peter Kerr, 12th Marquess of Lothian, and great-grandfather of Michael Kerr, 13th Marquess of Lothian. Lord Lothian died in November 1841 at the age of 47. After his death, the Marchioness converted to Catholicism with her two younger sons, Lord Ralph Kerr and Lord Walter Kerr, and her daughters. The Marchioness of Lothian died in May 1877, aged 69.
